title: A Greek Tragedy
subtitle: Thus, people make the choices they ought to make, and walk the paths they ought to walk.

trails.title: A Trail in the Forest
trails.description: Omens of fate hidden between the lines. Read, a voice says, the moment of choice has arrived.

content.text:
A fate has been forged for this purpose,
A maxim, a preconception,
A deliberate contemplation, a step taken.
Believed to be a choice.

The woodland is older than all within it.
Through passion, or reason,
Travelers grope and stumble through the branches,
Or silently tread the narrow path,
Or choose to turn away,
Stepping into the subtle unknown.

Read, the voice urges.
If now, without pursuit, close to truth,
Yet let go.
Then never before had it been.

Step forward. So they say.
Before the tale is told, all is decided,
Merchants, competitors, mortals, and heroes.
And as the feast begins,
How shall they fade away.

And those outside,
For whom the time they've made has not yet come,
Those who deem themselves transcendent,
Are merely not in this procession.

items.text: A Greek Tragedy

The world is a door,
To a thousand ruins, desolate and cold.
For those who have lost,
What you have lost are long in the void.

                 —Vereinsamt by Friedrich Nietzsche
The flames of war rage along the shore.
Humans, Manus Vindictae, and Apeiron believers, all consumed by madness. The paints from their storm syndrome have bled into the sea, creating a disordered mixture of colors.
The flash of artillery and the glow of arcanum collide. Dead, infected sea creatures litter the shore, like a tableau of an abstract painting.

items.speaker: Marta
items.text: Where are you going, 37?
The sightless woman inquires with concern. Under her care, the leader's bleeding has finally ceased.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Please take care of 6 for me, Madam Marta.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I have to go find Sophia!
Not caring about anything else, she runs into the smoke.
Gunfire and explosions fill the air. The angry battle cries of former Apeiron believers, now in Manus attire, echo in all directions.

items.speaker: Manus Believer I
items.text: Die, humans!!!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Uhm!
The explosion knocks her off balance. She stumbles onto the gravel.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: *winces in pain*
A pair of hands reaches out to her.
Are you alright, 37? Can you get on your feet?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Ah! Sophia!
Finally. The voice she's been searching for fills her with relief.
She happily reaches for her hands, but stops abruptly, uncertain.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Did you change your clothes?
She pushes down the cacophony of emotions swelling inside her.
Where to begin?

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I have found my number, 37.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Your calculation was correct. As always.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: You found it? That's good!
She accepts the news without hesitation, her face lighting up with a genuine smile.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I always wanted to tell you. It is a great number, the number of a herald, prophet, and pioneer.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: When it was first discovered, mathematics was nearly destroyed. But luckily, it also spurred advancements in the field.
She stops, no longer rambling on about numbers, and sincerely gazes into her friend's emerald eyes.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Are we still friends, Sophia?
Sophia smiles. Smiling that she's still the same, even now.
She knows so much, yet she knows so little.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Yes, 37. We still are.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: But there are more important matters I must tend to.
A bomber howls over their heads, the pilot laughing hysterically.
The plane is covered in thick layers of paint, its wings curled and twisted.

items.speaker: Soldier I
items.text: Hahahahaha! This is ours! The land we discovered!
The pilot has spotted the two targets on the barren rocks below, with two explosives prepared for release.
Sophia does not flinch or retreat, instead her fingers wrap gently around the tiny idol.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Διορθωθεί το σφάλμα!
The bomber detonates in the sky, taking the young pilot with it.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Sophia, your power, and your look ...

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I must leave now, 37.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Lady Arcana has shown me another path.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: No. NO!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Why are you leaving, too? Is it because our circle has been broken?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: But I found the Truth!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I have the final solution! Just give me a little more time, and everything will be fine again, I promise!
She closes her eyes, the scripture still lingers in her mind.

"There are three kinds of people who come to the Olympic Games."
                 "The lowest class is made up of those who come to buy and sell, 
                   and the next above them are those who come to compete."
                 "But the most esteemed, however, are those who come to look on."
"Only these wise pursuers of knowledge ..."
"... may release themselves from the 'wheel of birth.'"

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: You and I are different, 37.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Not all of us have the privilege to look on from the sidelines.
She clenches the tiny idol.
A thick, tar-like substance seeps out from her body. In an instant, the bombers are wiped out completely.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Sophia, you ...
She can't prolong the inevitable any longer, she knows that.
This is the last thing she wants.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I will join Manus Vindictae, take others with me, and leave.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I will renounce the Scripture and seek vengeance in the phenomenal world.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Make your move, 37.
Tears roll down her eyes.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: If you really are the genius who can overcome anything ...

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Prove it to me.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Stop me, transcend me, defeat me …

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Crush me to dust.
The explosions have finally ceased.
The planes rest alongside the geometric bodies in the sea, sinking into an everlasting sleep.
The roars of battle are no more.
All that remains is the crashing of the waves against the shore.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Why?

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Why did you spare me, 37? Why did you show mercy? You weren't supposed to—
The battle ended quickly. 37's geometric brilliance has left only a tear on her friend's robe.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Because I don't want to fight you, Sophia!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Why? Why do we have to do this?!
Her voice is filled with anguish.
Sophia looks down in a long silence.
Then, she gently shakes her head.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I'm sorry, 37. I have gone beyond reason, beyond cure.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I must've been out of my mind to make you fight me. Your hands were never meant for violence. They were meant for upholding the Truth.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: As for me—I'm the one who clears the dust off the path, as fate foretold.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Goodbye, my beloved friend.
She no longer wavers or looks back.
Her shoulders tremble, but she strides toward the Manus with determination.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: It is time.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Please "clean up" the beach as quickly as possible. We will depart soon, as Lady Arcana has instructed.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Soph- ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Ms. Sophia!
The team is finally reunited.
Sonetto arrives last, heaving from trying to catch up to the scene.
She had her own battles elsewhere on the island. That strange dream has taken its toll on her.
And now she is holding her pen, silently questioning Sophia with a piercing stare.
Why?

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: We all have our own purpose to fulfill, Ms. Sonetto.
She walks right past her.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I will not fight you this time. But I will draw steel the next we meet.
The new members of the Manus Vindictae have left.
They did clean up the beach—every trace of humanity has been wiped clean.
Only rock and metal debris remain on the beach.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I don't understand any of this.
She slumps to the ground and stares blankly into the distance.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: The Truth transcends all and is above all trivial matters of the phenomenal world.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: It guides us to enlightenment and protects us from evil and misfortune, does it not?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: This is what I have always believed, so I went seeking for it. It is finally in my hands. But now, but now ...
37 buries her face between her knees, on the verge of sobbing.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: What went wrong? Was it my fault? Isn't this how the Truth is supposed to work?
It is not an easy question for an off-island visitor to answer.
However, one thing is for certain.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The Truth has not abandoned you, 37.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You haven't used the key yet, have you? It is still coded.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: The key ...
37 is helped up from the ground.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Lilya has verified Arcana's location. She is still on this island.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We still have a chance to stop her before it's truly too late.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We should go now, Sonetto.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We have 15 more hours until the "Storm."
TO BE CONTINUED…
